Karim

Overview

Karim serves Rindeil and formerly performed on stage. He tells Kir about a red-skinned youth once held by the scholars and locates a report in the necromancers’ citadel. Karim bribes a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the plan fails. Kir and Kel nevertheless retrieve the report, which points Kir toward another Joon. [1, 2, 3]

Shelter at Rindeil’s estate

Rindeil welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. Karim, who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, remembers a report about a red-skinned youth and promises to investigate. Rindeil’s hospitality gives the fugitives a base, but Kir realises that the slave records still identify them. With Rindeil’s guidance, he steals the records from the authorities. This removes one immediate threat without concealing his conspicuous appearance. [4, 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11]

Records and a new disguise

Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. Feiruz proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. [11, 12, 5, 13, 14, 15]

The meteorite and Feiruz’s favour

Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. [6, 16, 17, 18, 19, 7, 20, 21, 22]

The report and the passage to Gipath

Karim locates a report about the missing red-skinned youth in the necromancers’ citadel. He has bribed a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the watch remains alert. Kir and Kel retrieve the document despite the failed arrangement, and Kir defends Karim when Kel blames him. The report records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia initially warns against joining the army, then has convincing enlistment papers forged while Kir empties her dangerous caches for her. Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. Sergeant puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them. [8, 2, 3, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29]
